Adolf Loos, an Austrian architect, made ornamentation sound like something practiced only by primitive peoples or criminal deviants. But even a <u>cursory</u> glance at history demonstrates that ornament has always played a role in architecture, whether on ancient Greek temples, Gothic cathedrals, Renaissance palazzos, or the Capitol in Washington DC. Indeed, it is often the nature of the ornament that distinguishes different historical periods.

The reason for the persistence of ornamentation in architecture is that, far from being superfluous, it performs several useful functions. With ornament, an architect could give meaning to a building not only by incorporating specific references to what goes on inside but also by simply dialing the intensity of its ornamentation up or down. For instance, the main entrance of the Philadelphia Board of Education Building is not merely larger than the service entrance, it is more elaborately decorated, topped by two winged female figures and a medallion containing what looks like a coat of arms. Without distinctive ornamentation, a building risks being less nuanced, but without meaningful ornament, it risks becoming meaningless.

sents.en: Adolf Loos, an Austrian architect, made ornamentation sound like something practiced only by primitive peoples or criminal deviants.
sents.ko: 오스트리아의 건축가 아돌프 로스는 장식을 원시 민족이나 범죄적 일탈자들만이 행하는 것처럼 들리게 만들었다.

sents.en: But even a cursory glance at history demonstrates that ornament has always played a role in architecture, whether on ancient Greek temples, Gothic cathedrals, Renaissance palazzos, or the Capitol in Washington DC.
sents.ko: 그러나 역사를 대충 훑어보기만 해도(cursory glance), 고대 그리스 신전이든 고딕 대성당이든 르네상스 궁전이든 워싱턴 DC의 국회의사당이든, 건축에서 장식이 항상 한몫을 해 왔음을 알 수 있다.

sents.en: Indeed, it is often the nature of the ornament that distinguishes different historical periods.
sents.ko: 실제로 서로 다른 역사적 시기를 구분 짓는 것은 흔히 장식의 성격이다.

sents.en: The reason for the persistence of ornamentation in architecture is that, far from being superfluous, it performs several useful functions.
sents.ko: 건축에서 장식이 계속 존속하는 이유는, 장식이 불필요하기는커녕 여러 유용한 기능을 수행하기 때문이다.

sents.en: With ornament, an architect could give meaning to a building not only by incorporating specific references to what goes on inside but also by simply dialing the intensity of its ornamentation up or down.
sents.ko: 건축가는 장식을 통해, 건물 내부에서 일어나는 일에 대한 구체적 언급을 넣을 수도 있고, 단순히 장식의 강도를 높이거나 낮춤으로써도 건물에 의미를 부여할 수 있었다.

sents.en: For instance, the main entrance of the Philadelphia Board of Education Building is not merely larger than the service entrance, it is more elaborately decorated, topped by two winged female figures and a medallion containing what looks like a coat of arms.
sents.ko: 예를 들어, 필라델피아 교육위원회 건물의 정문은 단지 업무용 출입구보다 큰 것만이 아니라 더 정교하게 장식되어 있는데, 그 위에는 두 날개 달린 여성상과 문장(紋章)처럼 보이는 것이 들어 있는 메달 모양 장식이 얹혀 있다.

sents.en: Without distinctive ornamentation, a building risks being less nuanced, but without meaningful ornament, it risks becoming meaningless.
sents.ko: 독특한 장식이 없으면 건물은 섬세한 뉘앙스가 떨어질 위험이 있고, 의미 있는 장식이 없으면 건물은 무의미해질 위험이 있다.

Marcus Junius Brutus’s decision to join the plot to assassinate Julius Caesar cannot be divorced from the legacy etched in his very bloodline. From his illustrious ancestor, Lucius Junius Brutus, flowed a fierce current of republican ideals and unflinching opposition to tyranny. This founding father of the Roman Republic played a pivotal role in expelling the last king and establishing a system built on freedom and shared power. The oath he instituted among senators, swearing to uphold these values and forbid the rise of another monarch, echoed through generations, resonating deeply within the soul of his descendant.

Therefore, the act of joining the conspiracy against Caesar, far from being a betrayal of Rome, was, for Brutus, a desperate but necessary defense of the Roman Republic and the freedom it had long upheld. He did not strike down a friend, but a potential tyrant, his hand guided by the ghosts of liberty-fighters and the whispers of his proud lineage. In that fateful moment, Brutus wasn’t just acting for himself, but for the very spirit of Rome at its best, echoing the oath coined by his forefather centuries ago, to never allow a dictator to regain control over the Republic to enslave its free and independent people.

sents.en: Marcus Junius Brutus’s decision to join the plot to assassinate Julius Caesar cannot be divorced from the legacy etched in his very bloodline.
sents.ko: 마르쿠스 유니우스 브루투스가 율리우스 카이사르 암살 음모에 가담하기로 한 결정은 그의 혈통 자체에 새겨진 유산과 떼어놓고 생각할 수 없다.

sents.en: From his illustrious ancestor, Lucius Junius Brutus, flowed a fierce current of republican ideals and unflinching opposition to tyranny.
sents.ko: 그의 저명한 조상 루키우스 유니우스 브루투스로부터 공화정의 이상과 폭정에 대한 굳건한 반대라는 거센 흐름이 이어져 내려왔다.

passages.text: Though science fiction prizes reason, it fears rationality that has lost its grounding in the human; in other words, rationality that no longer arises from within human cognition. In science fiction films that feature supercomputers — such as Skynet in the Terminator films (1984-2009) or Arnim Zola in Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014) — the human is in danger of being replaced with the technological, and the computer represents the super-storehouse or ultimate embodiment of knowledge. Yet this, albeit writ large, reflects life in the “real” world as it is lived today. As information grows more and more disembodied, humans must, by necessity, interface with machines in order to function. Consequently, traditional notions of “the human” fall into <u>obsolescence</u> as people become “posthuman.” This means that being human is defined in terms of a new context — our interaction with artificially intelligent machines. In the posthuman world, humans have become less distinguishable from cyborgs or computers. In the contemporary landscape of computers, the Internet, and cyberspace, science fiction has become less and less fictional.

sents.en: Though science fiction prizes reason, it fears rationality that has lost its grounding in the human; in other words, rationality that no longer arises from within human cognition.
sents.ko: 공상과학은 이성을 높이 평가하면서도, 인간에 뿌리를 두는 기반을 잃은 합리성, 즉 더 이상 인간의 인지 내부에서 생겨나지 않는 합리성을 두려워한다.

sents.en: In science fiction films that feature supercomputers — such as Skynet in the Terminator films (1984-2009) or Arnim Zola in Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014) — the human is in danger of being replaced with the technological, and the computer represents the super-storehouse or ultimate embodiment of knowledge.

Conspiracy theorists dismiss “the Man from Stratford” as an imposter. They suppose that he was an <u>Ⓐilliterate</u> actor mouthing some nobler man’s words, somehow able to memorize lines despite his ignorance. The truth of the Authorship Controversy is that it is an <u>Ⓑoffshoot</u> of the cult of Shakespeare that emerged with the Romantic movement of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. Before that time, no one had any doubts about Shakespeare’s identity as the author of the plays of William Shakespeare. However, once he had been turned into a god, sects and heretics naturally emerged, eager to pull him down.

In point of fact, however, William Shakespeare was neither a fabulous aristocrat nor a <u>Ⓒflamboyant</u> double agent. Indeed, he came from a <u>Ⓓprovidential</u> town in middle England where he attended grammar school. As he grew, his primary concern became keeping out of trouble and bettering himself and his family. Perhaps that he came from a perfectly unremarkable background is the most remarkable thing of all. Maybe it was because Shakespeare was a nobody that he could become everybody. He speaks to every nation in every age because he understood what it is to be human. He didn’t lead the life of a <u>Ⓔpampered</u> aristocrat. He was a working craftsman who had to make his daily living and face the problems working people face every day. His life was ordinary; it was his mind that was extraordinary. His imagination leaped to distant lands and ages past, through fantasy and dream, yet it was always rooted in the real.

sents.en: Conspiracy theorists dismiss “the Man from Stratford” as an imposter.
sents.ko: 음모론자들은 '스트랫퍼드 출신의 사나이'를 사기꾼이라고 일축한다.

sents.en: They suppose that he was an Ⓐilliterate actor mouthing some nobler man’s words, somehow able to memorize lines despite his ignorance.
sents.ko: 그들은 그가 어떤 더 고귀한 사람의 말을 입으로만 읊는 Ⓐ글을 모르는(illiterate) 배우였으며, 무지한데도 어떻게든 대사를 외울 수 있었다고 생각한다.

sents.en: The truth of the Authorship Controversy is that it is an Ⓑoffshoot of the cult of Shakespeare that emerged with the Romantic movement of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.
sents.ko: 저작권 논쟁의 진실은, 그것이 18세기 후반과 19세기 초 낭만주의 운동과 함께 등장한 셰익스피어 숭배의 Ⓑ부산물(offshoot)이라는 것이다.

sents.en: Before that time, no one had any doubts about Shakespeare’s identity as the author of the plays of William Shakespeare.
sents.ko: 그 시기 이전에는 누구도 윌리엄 셰익스피어의 희곡들의 저자가 셰익스피어라는 점을 의심하지 않았다.

sents.ko: 그러나 그가 신의 지위에 올려지자, 그를 끌어내리고 싶어 하는 종파와 이단자들이 자연스럽게 생겨났다.

sents.ko: 그러나 사실, 윌리엄 셰익스피어는 엄청난 귀족도, Ⓒ화려하고 눈에 띄는(flamboyant) 이중간첩도 아니었다.

sents.en: Indeed, he came from a Ⓓprovidential town in middle England where he attended grammar school.
sents.ko: 실제로 그는 문법학교를 다닌 잉글랜드 중부의 Ⓓ신의 섭리에 의한(providential) 마을 출신이었다.

sents.ko: 성장하면서 그의 주된 관심사는 말썽에 휘말리지 않고 자신과 가족의 형편을 나아지게 하는 것이 되었다.

In the twenty-first century, we tend to associate the word “digital” with computation, but its origins <u>Ⓐhark back to</u> ancient times. The term derives from digitus in classical Latin, meaning “finger,” and later from digit, which refers to whole numbers less than ten as well as to fingers or toes. Digital procedures long <u>Ⓑpostdate</u> the development of electronic computers, as we might understand a number of earlier devices or systems as operating using digital principles. For instance, the abacus is a simple digital calculator dating from 300 BCE; furthermore, Morse code and Braille represent more recent digital practices. What each of these examples has in common is their use of the word “digital” to refer to discrete elements or separate numbers. This focus on the discrete and the separate is central to the functioning of today’s digital electronics, which, at a basic level, operate by distinguishing between two values: zero and one.

While the digital anticipated computation, today the two terms are closely linked, and the adjective “digital” is typically a <u>Ⓒshorthand for</u> the binary systems that <u>Ⓓunderpin</u> computation. Thus we are living through a “digital revolution,” are at risk of an increasing “digital divide,” and are plugged into “digital devices” that play “digital audio” and store our “digital photographs.” Some of us even practice “digital humanities.” The <u>Ⓔslippage between</u> the digital and computation seems so complete that it is easy to assume that the two terms are and always have been synonymous.

sents.en: In the twenty-first century, we tend to associate the word “digital” with computation, but its origins Ⓐhark back to ancient times.
sents.ko: 21세기에 우리는 '디지털'이라는 단어를 계산과 연관 짓는 경향이 있지만, 그 기원은 고대로 Ⓐ거슬러 올라간다(hark back).

sents.en: The term derives from digitus in classical Latin, meaning “finger,” and later from digit, which refers to whole numbers less than ten as well as to fingers or toes.
sents.ko: 이 용어는 '손가락'을 뜻하는 고전 라틴어 digitus에서 유래했고, 이후 손가락이나 발가락뿐 아니라 10 미만의 정수를 가리키는 digit에서 나왔다.

sents.en: Digital procedures long Ⓑpostdate the development of electronic computers, as we might understand a number of earlier devices or systems as operating using digital principles.
sents.ko: 디지털 방식은 전자 컴퓨터의 발전보다 훨씬 Ⓑ앞서 있었는데(원문은 postdate), 우리는 이전의 여러 장치나 체계가 디지털 원리를 사용해 작동했다고 이해할 수 있다.

sents.en: For instance, the abacus is a simple digital calculator dating from 300 BCE; furthermore, Morse code and Braille represent more recent digital practices.
sents.ko: 예를 들어 주판은 기원전 300년경으로 거슬러 올라가는 단순한 디지털 계산기이며, 나아가 모스 부호와 점자는 더 최근의 디지털 관행을 나타낸다.

sents.en: What each of these examples has in common is their use of the word “digital” to refer to discrete elements or separate numbers.
sents.ko: 이 예들 각각의 공통점은 '디지털'이라는 단어를 이산적인 요소나 별개의 숫자를 가리키는 데 쓴다는 점이다.

sents.en: This focus on the discrete and the separate is central to the functioning of today’s digital electronics, which, at a basic level, operate by distinguishing between two values: zero and one.
sents.ko: 이처럼 이산적인 것과 분리된 것에 초점을 두는 것은 오늘날 디지털 전자기기의 작동 방식의 핵심인데, 이 기기들은 기본 수준에서 0과 1이라는 두 값을 구별하는 방식으로 작동한다.

sents.en: While the digital anticipated computation, today the two terms are closely linked, and the adjective “digital” is typically a Ⓒshorthand for the binary systems that Ⓓunderpin computation.
sents.ko: 디지털이 계산을 앞서 예고했지만, 오늘날 두 용어는 밀접하게 연결되어 있으며, 형용사 '디지털'은 대개 계산을 Ⓓ뒷받침하는(underpin) 이진 체계의 Ⓒ약칭(shorthand)이다.

sents.en: Thus we are living through a “digital revolution,” are at risk of an increasing “digital divide,” and are plugged into “digital devices” that play “digital audio” and store our “digital photographs.”
sents.ko: 그리하여 우리는 '디지털 혁명'을 겪고 있고, 점점 커지는 '디지털 격차'의 위험에 처해 있으며, '디지털 오디오'를 재생하고 '디지털 사진'을 저장하는 '디지털 기기'에 연결되어 있다.

sents.en: Some of us even practice “digital humanities.”
sents.ko: 우리 중 일부는 심지어 '디지털 인문학'을 하기도 한다.

sents.en: The Ⓔslippage between the digital and computation seems so complete that it is easy to assume that the two terms are and always have been synonymous.
sents.ko: 디지털과 계산 사이의 Ⓔ미끄러짐(slippage, 의미의 변이)은 너무나 완전해 보여서, 두 용어가 동의어이고 항상 동의어였다고 가정하기 쉽다.

passages.text:
John Searle, the eminent American philosopher of language, introduced the concept of “the principle of expressibility,” which posits the fundamental nature of human thought in its relationship to language. This principle asserts that any thought capable of being articulated in one language can be expressed just as <u>succinctly</u> in any other. At its core, this concept proposes that thought transcends the limitations of specific languages and operates within an abstract, universal realm.

Searle’s notion challenges the boundaries imposed by linguistic determinism, suggesting that beneath the multitude of spoken languages lies a common substrate of thought — a universal language of the mind that operates independently of words. This language of thought is purely conceptual, residing in the abstract realm of ideas and concepts, devoid of the constraints imposed by linguistic structures.

From Searle’s perspective, the languages we speak serve as vehicles that embody and carry our thoughts. They act as tools to convey the rich tapestry of abstract ideas formulated within the language of thought. Thus, while the language of thought itself remains inaccessible and <u>ineffable</u>, our spoken languages serve as conduits through which we attempt to convey and articulate the vast complexities of our internal mental landscapes.

sents.en: John Searle, the eminent American philosopher of language, introduced the concept of “the principle of expressibility,” which posits the fundamental nature of human thought in its relationship to language.
sents.ko: 저명한 미국의 언어철학자 존 설은 인간 사고의 근본적 성격이 언어와의 관계에 있다고 상정하는 '표현 가능성의 원리'라는 개념을 도입했다.

sents.en: This principle asserts that any thought capable of being articulated in one language can be expressed just as succinctly in any other.
sents.ko: 이 원리는 한 언어로 표현될 수 있는 어떤 생각이든 다른 어떤 언어로도 똑같이 간결하게(succinctly) 표현될 수 있다고 주장한다.

sents.en: At its core, this concept proposes that thought transcends the limitations of specific languages and operates within an abstract, universal realm.
sents.ko: 근본적으로 이 개념은 사고가 특정 언어의 한계를 초월하여 추상적이고 보편적인 영역 안에서 작동한다고 제안한다.

sents.en: Searle’s notion challenges the boundaries imposed by linguistic determinism, suggesting that beneath the multitude of spoken languages lies a common substrate of thought — a universal language of the mind that operates independently of words.
sents.ko: 설의 개념은 언어결정론이 부과하는 경계에 도전하며, 수많은 구어들 아래에는 공통의 기저인 사고, 곧 단어와 무관하게 작동하는 보편적인 마음의 언어가 놓여 있음을 시사한다.

sents.en: This language of thought is purely conceptual, residing in the abstract realm of ideas and concepts, devoid of the constraints imposed by linguistic structures.
sents.ko: 이 사고의 언어는 순전히 개념적이어서 관념과 개념의 추상적 영역에 머물며, 언어 구조가 부과하는 제약이 없다.

sents.en: From Searle’s perspective, the languages we speak serve as vehicles that embody and carry our thoughts.
sents.ko: 설의 관점에서, 우리가 말하는 언어들은 우리의 생각을 구현하고 실어 나르는 수단 역할을 한다.

sents.en: They act as tools to convey the rich tapestry of abstract ideas formulated within the language of thought.
sents.ko: 언어들은 사고의 언어 안에서 형성된 추상적 관념의 풍부한 직조물을 전달하는 도구로 기능한다.

sents.en: Thus, while the language of thought itself remains inaccessible and ineffable, our spoken languages serve as conduits through which we attempt to convey and articulate the vast complexities of our internal mental landscapes.
sents.ko: 따라서 사고의 언어 자체는 접근할 수 없고 말로 표현할 수 없는(ineffable) 채로 남아 있지만, 우리의 구어는 우리가 내면의 정신적 풍경의 방대한 복잡성을 전달하고 표현하려고 시도하는 통로로 기능한다.

passages.text:
Dr. Karl Menninger, a pioneering psychiatrist and authority on criminal psychology, proposes upending the traditional “punishment for crime” model underlying criminal justice in America. Unlike the retributive justice system which emphasizes punishment, Menninger proposed focusing on the offender, advocating for treatment and rehabilitation instead of simply fitting the punishment to the offense.

Driven by a holistic view of well-being that posits total health as the way to true rehabilitation, Menninger championed humane therapy and rejected labeling individuals as “insane.” In his book The Crime of Punishment, he condemned all forms of punishment, including imprisonment and capital punishment, as cruel and ineffective. He believed punishment fails both individuals and society, specifically by neglecting the mental health needs of prisoners.

Menninger’s approach resonates with inmates and continues to inform calls for criminal justice reform. Instead of rigid punishment based solely on the crime, his philosophy pushes for individualized treatment and rehabilitation plans, promoting empathy and understanding over vengeance. This shift in perspective challenges us to rethink how we handle crime, prioritizing rehabilitation and the unique needs of each individual involved.

sents.en: Dr. Karl Menninger, a pioneering psychiatrist and authority on criminal psychology, proposes upending the traditional “punishment for crime” model underlying criminal justice in America.
sents.ko: 선구적인 정신과 의사이자 범죄 심리학의 권위자인 칼 메닝거 박사는 미국 형사 사법의 토대가 되는 전통적인 '범죄에 대한 처벌' 모델을 뒤엎자고 제안한다.

sents.en: Unlike the retributive justice system which emphasizes punishment, Menninger proposed focusing on the offender, advocating for treatment and rehabilitation instead of simply fitting the punishment to the offense.
sents.ko: 처벌을 강조하는 응보적 사법 제도와 달리, 메닝거는 단순히 범죄에 맞는 처벌을 하는 대신 치료와 재활을 옹호하며 범죄자에 초점을 맞출 것을 제안했다.

sents.en: Driven by a holistic view of well-being that posits total health as the way to true rehabilitation, Menninger championed humane therapy and rejected labeling individuals as “insane.”
sents.ko: 전반적 건강이 진정한 재활로 가는 길이라고 보는 총체적인 안녕관에 이끌려, 메닝거는 인도적인 치료를 옹호했고 사람들에게 '정신이상자'라는 낙인을 찍는 것을 거부했다.

sents.en: In his book The Crime of Punishment, he condemned all forms of punishment, including imprisonment and capital punishment, as cruel and ineffective.
sents.ko: 그의 저서 《처벌이라는 범죄》에서 그는 투옥과 사형을 포함한 모든 형태의 처벌을 잔인하고 비효과적이라며 비난했다.

sents.ko: 그는 처벌이 개인과 사회 모두를 실패하게 한다고 믿었는데, 특히 수감자들의 정신 건강 요구를 외면하기 때문이라고 보았다.

sents.en: Menninger’s approach resonates with inmates and continues to inform calls for criminal justice reform.
sents.ko: 메닝거의 접근 방식은 수감자들에게 공감을 얻고 있으며 형사 사법 개혁 요구에 계속 영향을 주고 있다.

sents.en: Instead of rigid punishment based solely on the crime, his philosophy pushes for individualized treatment and rehabilitation plans, promoting empathy and understanding over vengeance.
sents.ko: 오로지 범죄에만 기반한 엄격한 처벌 대신, 그의 철학은 개인별 치료와 재활 계획을 추진하며 복수보다 공감과 이해를 장려한다.

sents.en: This shift in perspective challenges us to rethink how we handle crime, prioritizing rehabilitation and the unique needs of each individual involved.
sents.ko: 이러한 관점의 전환은 우리가 범죄를 다루는 방식을 다시 생각하고, 재활과 관련된 각 개인의 고유한 필요를 우선시하도록 도전한다.

passages.text:
In the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, European-style grand hotel bars, such as those at Colombo’s Galle Face and Singapore’s Raffles hotels, played an important role in British colonial life. In their heyday these establishments strove to offer their guests a taste of home. Today, however, we can look back and see in them a microcosm of the broader imperial narrative, one that reflected the changing times in which such hotel bars thrived.

At that time, traditional gender norms were giving way to the shifting social dynamics then underway in Britain and the western world. For example, the debut of the “Singapore Sling” cocktail at Raffles Hotel — a seemingly small change — disrupted the tradition of the colonial bar as a male-only space. For, as cocktails were then considered drinks appropriate for women yet unsuitable for men, this change was likely instituted in anticipation of welcoming female patrons into bars in defiance of longstanding social taboos.

Furthermore, the bars in colonial grand hotels revealed the state of racial tensions in the colonial period. Despite a veneer of inclusion — and, in fact, being owned and operated by Arab, Jewish, and Arminian entrepreneurs — the maintenance of race-based distinctions, while complicated, was upheld in colonial hotel bars. For, while superficially welcoming a diverse clientele and claiming no restrictions, the grand hotel barrooms nevertheless discreetly adhered to longstanding racial hierarchies. In other words, racial restrictions were not overtly imposed, but covertly. For instance, Eurasian patrons were typically subjected to subtle forms of segregation, such as in seating or in quality of service.

In conclusion, colonial hotels, being progressive yet exclusionary, integrated yet discriminatory, encapsulated the paradoxes and hypocrisies of their times. They endure as historical witnesses, revealing the then ongoing struggles over gender norms and racial divisions in existence at a time when the world was in the process of slowly changing.

sents.en: In the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, European-style grand hotel bars, such as those at Colombo’s Galle Face and Singapore’s Raffles hotels, played an important role in British colonial life.
sents.ko: 18세기 후반과 19세기 초에, 콜롬보의 갈레 페이스 호텔과 싱가포르의 래플스 호텔에 있던 것 같은 유럽식 대형 호텔 바는 영국 식민지 생활에서 중요한 역할을 했다.

sents.en: In their heyday these establishments strove to offer their guests a taste of home.
sents.ko: 전성기에 이 시설들은 투숙객에게 고향의 맛을 제공하려고 애썼다.

sents.en: Today, however, we can look back and see in them a microcosm of the broader imperial narrative, one that reflected the changing times in which such hotel bars thrived.
sents.ko: 그러나 오늘날 우리는 되돌아보며 그것들에서 더 넓은 제국 서사의 축소판, 즉 그러한 호텔 바가 번성하던 시대의 변화를 반영한 서사를 볼 수 있다.

sents.en: At that time, traditional gender norms were giving way to the shifting social dynamics then underway in Britain and the western world.
sents.ko: 당시 전통적인 성별 규범은 영국과 서구 세계에서 진행되던 변화하는 사회적 역학에 자리를 내주고 있었다.

sents.en: For example, the debut of the “Singapore Sling” cocktail at Raffles Hotel — a seemingly small change — disrupted the tradition of the colonial bar as a male-only space.
sents.ko: 예를 들어, 래플스 호텔에서 '싱가포르 슬링' 칵테일이 첫선을 보인 것은 겉보기에는 작은 변화였지만 식민지 바가 남성 전용 공간이라는 전통을 흔들어 놓았다.

sents.en: For, as cocktails were then considered drinks appropriate for women yet unsuitable for men, this change was likely instituted in anticipation of welcoming female patrons into bars in defiance of longstanding social taboos.
sents.ko: 왜냐하면 당시 칵테일은 여성에게는 적합하지만 남성에게는 부적합한 음료로 여겨졌으므로, 이 변화는 오랜 사회적 금기를 거스르고 여성 손님을 바에 맞이하는 것을 예상하고 도입되었을 가능성이 높기 때문이다.

sents.en: Furthermore, the bars in colonial grand hotels revealed the state of racial tensions in the colonial period.
sents.ko: 게다가 식민지 대형 호텔의 바는 식민지 시대의 인종적 긴장 상태를 드러냈다.

sents.en: Despite a veneer of inclusion — and, in fact, being owned and operated by Arab, Jewish, and Arminian entrepreneurs — the maintenance of race-based distinctions, while complicated, was upheld in colonial hotel bars.
sents.ko: 겉으로는 포용적인 모습을 띠었고 실제로 아랍인, 유대인, 아르메니아인 사업가들이 소유하고 운영했음에도 불구하고, 복잡하긴 했지만 인종에 기반한 구분의 유지가 식민지 호텔 바에서는 지켜졌다.

sents.ko: 예를 들어 유라시아계 손님들은 대개 좌석 배정이나 서비스 품질 같은 면에서 미묘한 형태의 분리를 겪었다.

sents.en: In conclusion, colonial hotels, being progressive yet exclusionary, integrated yet discriminatory, encapsulated the paradoxes and hypocrisies of their times.
sents.ko: 결론적으로 식민지 호텔은 진보적이면서 배타적이고, 통합적이면서 차별적이어서 그 시대의 역설과 위선을 압축적으로 보여 주었다.

sents.en: They endure as historical witnesses, revealing the then ongoing struggles over gender norms and racial divisions in existence at a time when the world was in the process of slowly changing.
sents.ko: 그것들은 역사의 증인으로 남아, 세상이 서서히 변해 가던 시기에 존재했던, 당시 진행 중이던 성별 규범과 인종 분열을 둘러싼 투쟁을 드러내 준다.

questions.stem: The literary utopias had fallen into ________ since St. Augustine’s era some thousand years earlier, but the publication of Sir Thomas More’s enduring classic revived the fortunes of the genre, becoming the fountain for the outpouring of what we now call utopias.

affluence
abeyance
aberration

questions.trans: 문학적 유토피아는 약 천 년 전 성 아우구스티누스 시대 이후 중단 상태에 빠져 있었으나, 토머스 모어 경의 불후의 고전이 출간되면서 이 장르의 운명이 되살아났고, 오늘날 우리가 유토피아라 부르는 작품들이 쏟아져 나오는 원천이 되었다.

sents.en: The literary utopias had fallen into ________ since St. Augustine’s era some thousand years earlier, but the publication of Sir Thomas More’s enduring classic revived the fortunes of the genre, becoming the fountain for the outpouring of what we now call utopias.

barracked

sents.en: The enraged mob _______ the government building, leaving a trail of broken glass and scattered files in their wake.

questions.stem: Psychologists and anthropologists assure us that the human psyche is ______, contrary to the popular conception that states “a leopard can’t change its spots.”
choices: alchemical
omniscient
monolithic
ostentatious
malleable
questions.explain: '표범은 자기 반점을 바꿀 수 없다(사람은 변하지 않는다)'는 통념과 반대(contrary to)이므로 인간 정신은 '변화 가능하다, 유연하다(malleable)'가 적절하다. monolithic(획일적이고 단단한)은 통념 쪽 의미다.
questions.trans: 심리학자와 인류학자들은 '표범은 자기 반점을 바꿀 수 없다'는 통념과 달리 인간의 정신은 변할 수 있다고(유연하다고) 단언한다.

sents.en: Psychologists and anthropologists assure us that the human psyche is ______, contrary to the popular conception that states “a leopard can’t change its spots.”
sents.ko: 심리학자들과 인류학자들은 '표범은 얼룩무늬를 바꿀 수 없다'는 통념과 달리 인간의 정신이 ( 빈칸: 변하기 쉽다 )고 우리에게 장담한다.

choices_ko: 연금술의, 변환의
전지(全知)의
단일체의, 획일적인
과시적인, 허세 부리는
가단성 있는, 순응성이 있는, 쉽게 변하는

questions.stem: Years of government research prove conclusively that young people are drawn to cigarette smoking by the image the product portrays through its packaging. Over the years, tobacco companies have spent billions of dollars on aggressive advertising associating their brand image with positive and successful lifestyles. Activists, realizing this, lobbied the government to require that cigarette packaging be made as unattractive as possible. Ultimately, to _______ smoking in the eyes of the young, laws were enacted forcing tobacco companies to package cigarettes as unattractively as possible, using off-putting colors and accompanied by images of diseased organs.
choices: disenthrall
disparage
disinterest
disincline
disinherit
questions.explain: 빈칸의 목적어는 사람이 아니라 'smoking(흡연이라는 행위)'이고, in the eyes of the young은 '젊은이들 눈에'라는 부사구다. 따라서 '사물을 목적어로 받아 깎아내리다'인 ② disparage가 맞다(disparage smoking). 나머지는 모두 '사람'을 목적어로 받는 동사라 구조가 안 맞는다: disenthrall sb (from A) 환상에서 깨어나게 하다 / disinterest sb (in A) ~에 흥미를 잃게 하다(주로 명사 '무관심') / disincline sb (to A) 내키지 않게 하다 / disinherit sb 상속권을 박탈하다. 예: disinterest the young in smoking은 가능하지만 disinterest smoking은 불가.
questions.trans: 결국 젊은이들의 눈에 흡연을 깎아내리기 위해, 담배 회사들이 혐오감을 주는 색을 쓰고 병든 장기 사진을 곁들여 최대한 매력 없이 담배를 포장하도록 강제하는 법이 제정되었다.

sents.en: Years of government research prove conclusively that young people are drawn to cigarette smoking by the image the product portrays through its packaging.
sents.ko: 수년간의 정부 연구는 젊은이들이 담배 포장이 보여 주는 이미지에 이끌려 흡연을 하게 된다는 것을 결정적으로 입증한다.

sents.en: Over the years, tobacco companies have spent billions of dollars on aggressive advertising associating their brand image with positive and successful lifestyles.
sents.ko: 수년에 걸쳐 담배 회사들은 자사의 브랜드 이미지를 긍정적이고 성공적인 생활방식과 연관 짓는 공격적인 광고에 수십억 달러를 써 왔다.

sents.en: Activists, realizing this, lobbied the government to require that cigarette packaging be made as unattractive as possible.
sents.ko: 이를 깨달은 활동가들은 담배 포장을 가능한 한 매력 없게 만들도록 요구하라고 정부에 로비했다.

sents.en: Ultimately, to _______ smoking in the eyes of the young, laws were enacted forcing tobacco companies to package cigarettes as unattractively as possible, using off-putting colors and accompanied by images of diseased organs.
sents.ko: 결국 젊은이들의 눈에 비친 흡연을 ( 빈칸: 깎아내리기 ) 위해, 담배 회사들이 거부감을 주는 색상을 쓰고 병든 장기의 이미지를 곁들여 담배를 가능한 한 매력 없게 포장하도록 강제하는 법이 제정되었다.

choices_ko: 환상에서 깨어나게 하다
폄하하다, 깎아내리다
(n.) 무관심 / (v.) ~의 흥미를 잃게 하다
내키지 않게 하다
상속권을 박탈하다

questions.stem: The economist analyzed the data from various sources to assess the overall economic performance of the region. Despite fluctuations in individual sectors, the figures revealed a stable growth trend. Understanding the importance of studying diverse data sets side by side, the researcher aimed to present potential investors with a comprehensive overview of the region’s economic landscape. By ________ information from different sources, a clearer picture emerged, which facilitated more informed decisions regarding his client’s future investment strategies.
choices: propagating
abnegating
variegating
aggregating
denigrating
questions.explain: 여러 출처의 데이터를 나란히 연구해 종합적 개관을 제시하려 했다는 맥락이므로 정보를 '모으다, 종합하다(aggregating)'가 정답이다. propagate(전파하다), variegate(얼룩덜룩하게 하다), denigrate(폄하하다)는 맞지 않는다.
questions.trans: 서로 다른 출처의 정보를 종합함으로써 더 명확한 그림이 드러났고, 이는 고객의 향후 투자 전략에 관해 더 정보에 입각한 결정을 내리는 데 도움이 되었다.

sents.en: The economist analyzed the data from various sources to assess the overall economic performance of the region.
sents.ko: 그 경제학자는 해당 지역의 전반적인 경제 성과를 평가하기 위해 여러 출처의 데이터를 분석했다.

sents.en: Despite fluctuations in individual sectors, the figures revealed a stable growth trend.
sents.ko: 개별 부문의 등락에도 불구하고 수치는 안정적인 성장 추세를 보여 주었다.

sents.en: Understanding the importance of studying diverse data sets side by side, the researcher aimed to present potential investors with a comprehensive overview of the region’s economic landscape.
sents.ko: 다양한 데이터 집합을 나란히 연구하는 것의 중요성을 이해하고 있던 그 연구자는 잠재적 투자자들에게 그 지역의 경제 지형에 대한 포괄적인 개관을 제시하고자 했다.

sents.en: By ________ information from different sources, a clearer picture emerged, which facilitated more informed decisions regarding his client’s future investment strategies.
sents.ko: 여러 출처의 정보를 ( 빈칸: 종합함 )으로써 더 명확한 그림이 드러났고, 이는 의뢰인의 향후 투자 전략에 대해 더 충분한 정보에 근거한 결정을 하는 데 도움이 되었다.

choices_ko: 번식시키다, 전파하다
(권리·신념을) 포기하다, 부인하다
다양하게 하다, 얼룩덜룩하게 하다
모으다, 종합하다
폄훼하다, 헐뜯다

B: But this time it’s just the bus fare. Oh, this is terrible!

choices_ko: B: 말도 안 돼! 6개월 전에 올랐잖아?
A: 응. 모든 대중교통 요금이 인상됐어.
B: 그런데 이번에는 버스 요금만 오르는 거잖아. 아, 너무하네!

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct according to the passage?
choices: Adolf Loos was enthusiastic about the use of ornamentation in architecture.
Ornamentation in architecture is always indicative of primitive culture.
The US Capitol is known for its ornamental entrances and exits.
Architectural ornamentation is becoming less and less fashionable.
The abandonment of ornamentation in architecture causes needless confusion.
questions.explain: 마지막 문장에서 의미 있는 장식이 없으면 건물이 무의미해질 위험이 있다고 하므로, 장식을 포기하면 불필요한 혼란(의미 상실)이 생긴다는 ⑤가 일치한다. Loos는 장식을 원시적인 것으로 여겼으므로 ①은 반대다.
questions.trans: 차별화된 장식이 없으면 건물은 덜 미묘해질 위험이 있지만, 의미 있는 장식이 없으면 무의미해질 위험이 있다.

sents.en: Which of the following is correct according to the passage?
sents.ko: 다음 중 지문에 따라 옳은 것은?

choices_ko: 아돌프 로스는 건축에서 장식을 사용하는 것에 열광했다.
건축의 장식은 언제나 원시 문화를 나타낸다.
미국 국회의사당은 장식적인 출입구로 유명하다.
건축 장식은 점점 유행에서 멀어지고 있다.
건축에서 장식을 버리면 불필요한 혼란이 생긴다.

questions.stem: The arrival of the Spanish in Mexico in 1521 marked the beginning of the transformation of the region’s cuisine, as the introduction of livestock — specifically cattle and pigs — <u>Ⓐprecipitating</u> the decline of the region’s traditional plant-centered diet. <u>ⒷTo reconnect with</u> their roots, a growing number of Mexicans and Mexican Americans are <u>Ⓒreadopting</u> traditional “plant-forward” eating habits. For example, one-time staples like maize, beans, and squash — known as the Three Sisters — <u>Ⓓnow feature</u> more prominently in everyday family meals. With such cooking making a resurgence, revivalists feel they are reclaiming a culinary tradition and <u>Ⓔpushing back</u> against colonialism by bringing back a narrative of heritage and sustainability.
questions.explain: as가 이끄는 절에 주어(the introduction of livestock)만 있고 본동사가 없으므로 Ⓐ precipitating은 precipitated가 되어야 한다.
questions.trans: 스페인인들이 1521년 멕시코에 도착하면서 이 지역 요리의 변화가 시작되었는데, 가축(특히 소와 돼지)의 도입이 이 지역의 전통적인 식물 중심 식단의 쇠퇴를 촉발했기 때문이다.

sents.en: The arrival of the Spanish in Mexico in 1521 marked the beginning of the transformation of the region’s cuisine, as the introduction of livestock — specifically cattle and pigs — Ⓐprecipitating the decline of the region’s traditional plant-centered diet.
sents.ko: 1521년 스페인인들이 멕시코에 도착한 것은 그 지역 음식 문화 변화의 시작을 알렸는데, 가축, 특히 소와 돼지의 도입이 그 지역의 전통적인 식물 중심 식단의 쇠퇴를 Ⓐ촉진했기 때문이다.

sents.en: ⒷTo reconnect with their roots, a growing number of Mexicans and Mexican Americans are Ⓒreadopting traditional “plant-forward” eating habits.
sents.ko: Ⓑ뿌리를 되찾기 위해 점점 더 많은 멕시코인과 멕시코계 미국인이 전통적인 '식물 중심' 식습관을 Ⓒ다시 받아들이고 있다.

sents.en: For example, one-time staples like maize, beans, and squash — known as the Three Sisters — Ⓓnow feature more prominently in everyday family meals.
sents.ko: 예를 들어 '세 자매'로 알려진 옥수수, 콩, 호박 같은 한때의 주식이 Ⓓ이제는 일상적인 가족 식사에서 더 두드러지게 등장한다.

sents.en: With such cooking making a resurgence, revivalists feel they are reclaiming a culinary tradition and Ⓔpushing back against colonialism by bringing back a narrative of heritage and sustainability.
sents.ko: 그러한 요리가 부활하면서, 복원 운동가들은 유산과 지속가능성의 서사를 되살림으로써 자신들이 요리 전통을 되찾고 식민주의에 Ⓔ맞서고 있다고 느낀다.

questions.stem: The capitalist ideology of abundance <u>Ⓐwas helping to</u> create a new cultural space, although several strong voices <u>Ⓑhad emerged to</u> contest it. It was an arena <u>Ⓒbeing filled with</u> commercial iconography and catchy slogans, with visions of goods and <u>Ⓓendlessly consumption</u>, with fashion shows and gaudy shop windows, with huge electrical billboards and mechanized displays <u>Ⓔtowering over</u> city streets.
questions.explain: 명사 consumption을 수식해야 하므로 부사 endlessly가 아니라 형용사 endless가 되어야 한다(Ⓓ). goods and endless consumption이 병렬을 이룬다.
questions.trans: 그곳은 상업적 도상과 귀에 쏙 들어오는 슬로건, 상품과 끝없는 소비의 환상, 패션쇼와 화려한 쇼윈도, 도시 거리 위로 우뚝 솟은 거대한 전광판과 기계식 진열로 채워지는 무대였다.

sents.en: The capitalist ideology of abundance Ⓐwas helping to create a new cultural space, although several strong voices Ⓑhad emerged to contest it.
sents.ko: 풍요의 자본주의 이데올로기는 새로운 문화 공간을 만드는 데 일조하고 Ⓐ있었지만, 여러 강력한 목소리가 그것에 이의를 제기하고 Ⓑ나선 상태였다.

sents.en: It was an arena Ⓒbeing filled with commercial iconography and catchy slogans, with visions of goods and Ⓓendlessly consumption, with fashion shows and gaudy shop windows, with huge electrical billboards and mechanized displays Ⓔtowering over city streets.
sents.ko: 그것은 상업적 도상과 귀에 쏙 들어오는 슬로건, 상품의 환상과 Ⓓ끝없는(endlessly: 문법상 endless가 맞음) 소비의 환상, 패션쇼와 번지르르한 상점 진열창, 도시 거리 위로 Ⓔ우뚝 솟은 거대한 전광판과 기계식 전시물로 Ⓒ채워지는 무대였다.

The effect of Brutus’s lineage on his response to the assassination plot
The threat Julius Caesar’s rule posed to the ideals of the Roman Republic
Reasons Brutus was considered just as much a tyrant as Caesar

choices_ko: 로마 왕정과 로마 공화정 사이의 주요 차이점
브루투스의 혈통이 암살 음모에 대한 그의 대응에 미친 영향

브루투스가 카이사르 못지않은 폭군으로 여겨진 이유

Brutus was a descendant of a founding father of the Roman Republic.

sents.ko: 지문에 따라 옳지 않은 것은?

choices_ko: 영국 식민지 호텔 바 문화는 영국 내 사회 진보를 선도했다.
콜롬보의 갈레 페이스 호텔과 싱가포르의 래플스 호텔은 '대형 호텔'로 불렸다.
식민지 대형 호텔 바는 자신들의 차별 관행을 위장하려 했다.
'싱가포르 슬링'은 래플스 호텔에서 처음에는 남성 바 손님을 겨냥한 것이 아니었을 가능성이 높다.
식민지 대형 호텔은 그 시대의 사회 변화 양상에 참여했다.

questions.trans: 결론적으로 식민지 호텔들은 진보적이면서도 배타적이고, 통합적이면서도 차별적이었다.

sents.en: What can be inferred from the passage?
sents.ko: 지문에서 추론할 수 있는 것은?

choices_ko: '싱가포르 슬링' 칵테일은 오로지 수익을 늘리기 위해 만들어졌다.
콜롬보와 싱가포르의 유라시아계 사람들은 호텔 바의 인종차별에 항의했다.
칵테일은 영국에서 식민지에서만큼 남성들에게 인기 없지는 않았다.
영국 식민지 바들이 받아들인 변화는 엇갈린 결과를 낳았다.
대형 호텔 체제로 돌아가면 사회 진보에 도움이 될 것이다.

questions.stem: Reorder the following sentences in the best way to form a coherent passage.
questions.box:
Ⓐ But there’s no actual written record of a city named Berlin until the 1240s.
Ⓑ Furthermore, it didn’t become a capital until 1701, when Prussian King Frederick the First declared it so and built the Charlottenburg Palace.
Ⓒ Whatever the case, the city has seen its fair share of history and been a center point of German culture for the greater part of a millennium.
Ⓓ Berlin is currently the capital of Germany, but no one quite knows when it was first settled.
Ⓔ There is evidence of a few buildings having existed there as far back as the late 1100s.
questions.explain: 도입 Ⓓ(베를린이 언제 처음 정착되었는지 아무도 모름) → Ⓔ(1100년대 후반 건물의 증거) → Ⓐ(But 1240년대까지 기록 없음) → Ⓑ(Furthermore 1701년에야 수도) → Ⓒ(Whatever the case 결론) 순서가 자연스럽다.
questions.trans: 베를린은 현재 독일의 수도이지만, 그곳에 언제 처음 사람들이 정착했는지는 아무도 정확히 알지 못한다.

sents.en: Reorder the following sentences in the best way to form a coherent passage.
sents.ko: 다음 문장들을 가장 알맞게 재배열하여 일관된 글이 되도록 하라.

sents.en: Ⓐ But there’s no actual written record of a city named Berlin until the 1240s.
sents.ko: Ⓐ 그러나 베를린이라는 도시에 대한 실제 문헌 기록은 1240년대가 되어서야 나타난다.

sents.en: Ⓑ Furthermore, it didn’t become a capital until 1701, when Prussian King Frederick the First declared it so and built the Charlottenburg Palace.
sents.ko: Ⓑ 게다가 베를린은 프로이센 왕 프리드리히 1세가 수도로 선포하고 샤를로텐부르크 궁전을 지은 1701년이 되어서야 수도가 되었다.

sents.en: Ⓒ Whatever the case, the city has seen its fair share of history and been a center point of German culture for the greater part of a millennium.
sents.ko: Ⓒ 어쨌든 이 도시는 상당한 역사를 겪었고 천 년에 가까운 세월의 대부분 동안 독일 문화의 중심지였다.

sents.en: Ⓓ Berlin is currently the capital of Germany, but no one quite knows when it was first settled.
sents.ko: Ⓓ 베를린은 현재 독일의 수도이지만, 언제 처음 정착이 이루어졌는지는 아무도 정확히 알지 못한다.

sents.en: Ⓔ There is evidence of a few buildings having existed there as far back as the late 1100s.
sents.ko: Ⓔ 그곳에 1100년대 후반까지 거슬러 올라가는 몇몇 건물이 존재했다는 증거가 있다.
